text.p: OFFICIAL NOTICE OF SALE
STATE OF GEORGIA
General Obligation Bonds, 1997C
SEALED BIDS will be received and publicly opened by the
undersigned at Suite 214, 254 Washington Street, Atlanta,
Georgia, at 11:00 O'Clock A.M. on Tuesday,
August 5, 1997
for all but no part of the above captioned bonds, dated
August 1, 1997. The bonds will be issued only as fully-
registered bonds in denominations of $5,000 each or any
whole multiple thereof. Both principal and semiannual
(February 1 and August 1) interest are payable at The Bank
of New York. The bonds mature on August 1 as follows:
THE BONDS OF THIS ISSUE ARE NONCALLABLE.
The bonds are issued by the Georgia State Financing and
Investment Commission for and on behalf of the State of
Georgia pursuant to powers granted to the Commission in the
Constitution of the State of Georgia, the Act creating the
Commission and an authorizing resolution of the Commission.
The bonds so issued constitute direct and general
obligations of the State of Georgia for the payment of which
the full faith, credit and taxing power of the State are
pledged.
Delivery of the bonds will be made in New York, New York
as soon as the bonds can be validated and prepared, which is
estimated to be August 28, 1997. However, the purchaser
shall allow 50 days for delivery. Payment for the bonds
shall be made in federal funds.
The bonds are offered subject to validation by the
Superior Court of Fulton County, Georgia, and delivery will
be accompanied by an execution, signature and no-litigation
certificate and non-arbitrage certificate. The legality of
the proceedings and the bonds will be approved by King &
Spalding, Atlanta, Georgia, the cost of whose approving
opinion shall be paid by the State. The legal opinion of
King & Spalding will be printed on the bonds.
Bidders may name the rate or rates of interest the bonds
are to bear in multiples of 1/20th of 1%, with no greater
difference than 4% between the highest and lowest rates
named and no interest rate shall exceed 6.25% per annum. All
bonds of each maturity must bear a single rate. No bid for
less than par and accrued interest will be considered.
Any bid providing for supplemental coupons will no
considered, and all bonds must bear interest to maturity.
The lowest and best bid will be determined by calculating
the total interest on all bonds from August 1, 1997 to date
of maturity, less any premium.
Instructions relating to certificate registration and
denominations must be forwarded so as to be received by the
Registrar Bank no later than August 22, 1997.
Within 48 hours after the award of the bonds, the
successful bidder shall submit to the Commission a
certificate, in form and substance satisfactory to Bond
Counsel, specifying for each maturity the expected bona fide
reoffering price of the bonds of each maturity, as of the
date of the award of the bid. Prior to delivery of the
bonds, the successful bidder must submit to the Commission a
certificate, in form and substance satisfactory to Bond
Counsel, stating that a bona fide offering of the bonds was
made to the public at the prices indicated in the first
certificate, certifying the actual reoffering price of at
least 10% of the bonds of each maturity, and identifying the
amounts, maturities, and prices at which any bonds were
actually sold to institutions or other investors at a
discount from the offering prices to the public. For
purposes of this paragraph, sales of bonds to other
securities brokers or dealers will not be counted as sales
to the public.
A Preliminary Official Statement for the bonds has been
prepared by the Commission. The Preliminary Official
Statement is deemed by the Commission to be final for the
purposes of compliance with Rule 15c2-12 of the Securities
and Exchange Commission. In order to assist bidders in
complying with Securities and Exchange Commission Rule 15c2-
12(b)(5) (the Rule''), the State will undertake, pursuant
to the resolution authorizing the issuance of the bonds and
a Continuing Disclosure Certificate, to provide annual
reports and notices of material events in accordance with
the provisions of the Rule. A form of the Continuing
Disclosure Certificate is set forth in Appendix E of the
Preliminary Official Statement and will be set forth in the
final Official Statement. The State's failure to deliver the
Continuing Disclosure Certificate on the date of issuance and delivery of the bonds shall relieve the successful
bidder of its obligation to purchase the bonds.
The Commission designates the senior managing underwriter
of the syndicate to which the bonds are awarded (the
Purchaser'') as its agent for purposes of distributing
copies of the final Official Statement to each participating
underwriter. Any underwriter executing and delivering a Bid
Form with respect to this issue agrees that, if its bid is
accepted by the Commission: (1) to accept such designation;
(2) to contact all participating underwriters for the
purpose of assuring proper dissemination of the final
Official Statement; and (3) to provide to the Commission,
within two (2) days after the date of the sale, all
necessary pricing information and underwriter identific
needed to complete the final Official Statement.
Upon receipt of this information, the Commission will
prepare and provide to the Purchaser, within seven (7)
business days after the sale, a sufficient number of copies
of the final Official Statement. The final Official
Statement will be in substantially the same form as the
preliminary document, subject to any additions, deletions,
or revisions that the Commission believes are necessary.
The right is reserved to reject any and all bids, and bids
shall be submitted upon the Bid Form furnished by the
Georgia State Financing and Investment Commission and
enclosed in a sealed envelope marked on the outside
PROPOSAL FOR 1997C BONDS.'' The Commission reserves the
right to waive informalities in any and all bids.
A good faith deposit in the amount of $2,404,400 shall be
made by each bidder in the form of a certified, treasurer's,
or cashier's check payable to the order of the Georgia State
Financing and Investment Commission. The deposit of the
successful bidder will be applied on the purchase price of
the bonds or retained by the Commission as liquidated
damages to it should the bidder fail to comply with the
terms of the bid. All checks of unsuccessful bidders will be
returned upon the acceptance of the successful bid, or with
24 hours. No interest will be paid on any good faith
deposit.
Preliminary Official Statements, including Notice of Sale
and Bid Form, have been mailed to a list of prospective
bidders and institutional investors. Further information and
details are available upon request from the Georgia State
Financing and Investment Commission, 254 Washington Street,
Suite 214, Atlanta, Georgia 30334 (telephone 404-656-2174).
